title: MC6809 interrupt and reset vectors
covers: The MC6809's vector locations at the top of memory: reset, NMI, the two software interrupts, SWI3, SWI2, FIRQ and IRQ

rows.text: The SWI3 vector location is FFF2 (MS byte) and FFF3 (LS byte).
SWI3 sets E, which the document glosses as the entire state being saved.
SWI3 stores to the stack, in this order, PCL, PCH, USL, USH, IYL, IYH, IXL, IXH, DPR, ACCB, ACCA and CCR.
Control is transferred through the SWI3 vector: PC takes the contents of FFF2 and FFF3.
All of the processor registers except the hardware stack pointer itself are pushed.
SWI3 does not mask (disable) the normal and fast interrupts.
The Condition Codes line of SWI3 reads: Not affected.
The addressing mode of SWI3 is inherent.
In the DISPATCH11 block, case 0x3F runs the SWI3 label, which stores VECTOR_SWI3 (0xFFF2 in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea.
INTERRUPT_VECTOR loads PC high and low from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), reading memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, but calls the bound vector callback instead when one is set.
The SWI3 label calls debugger_exception_hook with EXCEPTION_SWI3.
SOFTWARE_INTERRUPT calls dummy_read_opcode_arg(0) and dummy_vma(1), and INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
The SWI2 vector location is FFF4 (MS byte) and FFF5 (LS byte).
SWI2 sets E, which the document glosses as the entire state being saved.
SWI2 stores to the stack, in this order, PCL, PCH, USL, USH, IYL, IYH, IXL, IXH, DPR, ACCB, ACCA and CCR.
Control is transferred through the SWI2 vector: PC takes the contents of FFF4 and FFF5.
All of the processor registers except the hardware stack pointer itself are pushed.
SWI2 does not mask (disable) the normal and fast interrupts.
SWI2 is available to the end user and must not be used in packaged software.
The Condition Codes line of SWI2 reads: Not affected.
The addressing mode of SWI2 is inherent.
In the DISPATCH10 block, case 0x3F runs the SWI2 label, which stores VECTOR_SWI2 (0xFFF4 in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea.
INTERRUPT_VECTOR loads PC high and low from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), reading memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, but calls the bound vector callback instead when one is set.
The SWI2 label calls debugger_exception_hook with EXCEPTION_SWI2.
SOFTWARE_INTERRUPT calls dummy_read_opcode_arg(0) and dummy_vma(1), and INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
In the DISPATCH10 block, case 0x3E runs XSWI2, which stores VECTOR_SWI2, calls the exception hook, selects S and pushes the entire state before INTERRUPT_VECTOR.
The SWI vector location is FFFA (MS byte) and FFFB (LS byte).
SWI sets E, which the document glosses as the entire state being saved.
SWI stores to the stack, in this order, PCL, PCH, USL, USH, IYL, IYH, IXL, IXH, DPR, ACCB, ACCA and CCR.
Control is transferred through the SWI vector: PC takes the contents of FFFA and FFFB.
All of the processor registers except the hardware stack pointer itself are pushed.
SWI sets I and F; the document says this masks (disables) both the normal and fast interrupts.
The Condition Codes line of SWI reads: Not affected.
The addressing mode of SWI is inherent.
In the DISPATCH01 block, case 0x3F runs the SWI label, which stores VECTOR_SWI (0xFFFA in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea.
SWI continues at INTERRUPT_VECTOR: PC high and low come from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, or the bound vector callback when one is set.
The SWI label calls debugger_exception_hook with EXCEPTION_SWI.
The SWI label calls dummy_read_opcode_arg(0) and dummy_vma(1), and INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
The FIRQ vector location is FFF6 (MS byte) and FFF7 (LS byte).
A FIRQ with the F bit clear causes the interrupt sequence to occur at the end of the current instruction.
The FIRQ sequence pushes the program counter (PCL, then PCH) and then the condition code register onto the hardware stack.
FIRQ clears E; the document glosses this as a subset of the state being saved.
FIRQ sets F and I; the document says this masks further interrupts, so a normal IRQ cannot interrupt the routine.
Program control is transferred through the FIRQ vector: PC takes the contents of FFF6 and FFF7.
The Condition Codes line of FIRQ reads: Not affected.
An RTI instruction returns the processor to the original task.
It is possible to enter the FIRQ routine with the entire machine state saved if FIRQ occurs after a clear and wait for interrupt instruction.
The mask bit I could be reset during the interrupt routine if priority was not desired.
FIRQ allows operations on memory, TST, INC, DEC and the like without the overhead of saving the entire machine state on the stack.
The addressing mode of FIRQ is inherent.
The FIRQ label stores VECTOR_FIRQ (0xFFF6 in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea; MAIN jumps to it when get_pending_interrupt returns VECTOR_FIRQ.
The label continues at INTERRUPT_VECTOR: PC high and low come from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, or the bound vector callback when one is set.
The FIRQ label calls standard_irq_callback with M6809_FIRQ_LINE and the PC.
The label calls dummy_read_opcode_arg(0) twice and dummy_vma(1) once, and INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
The FIRQ label saves the entire state with E set when firq_saves_entire_state() is true; m6809.h defines that function as returning false.
The IRQ vector location is FFF8 (MS byte) and FFF9 (LS byte).
If the I bit is clear, a low level on the IRQ input causes the interrupt sequence to occur at the end of the current instruction.
IRQ stores to the stack, in this order, PCL, PCH, USL, USH, IYL, IYH, IXL, IXH, DPR, ACCB, ACCA and CCR.
IRQ sets E, which the document glosses as the entire state being saved.
IRQ sets I; the document says this masks further IRQ interrupts.
Program control is transferred through the IRQ vector: PC takes the contents of FFF8 and FFF9.
The Condition Codes line of IRQ reads: Not affected.
Control is returned to the interrupted program using an RTI instruction.
A FIRQ may interrupt a normal IRQ routine and be recognized anytime after the interrupt vector is taken.
The addressing mode of IRQ is inherent.
The IRQ label stores VECTOR_IRQ (0xFFF8 in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea; MAIN jumps to it when get_pending_interrupt returns VECTOR_IRQ.
The label continues at INTERRUPT_VECTOR: PC high and low come from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, or the bound vector callback when one is set.
The IRQ label calls standard_irq_callback with M6809_IRQ_LINE and the PC.
The label calls dummy_read_opcode_arg(0) twice and dummy_vma(1) once, and INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
The RESET vector location is FFFE (MS byte) and FFFF (LS byte).
RESTART gives CCR the value X1X1XXXX: the second and fourth characters are 1 (the capture lost the arrow).
RESTART sets DPR to 0016, read here as hexadecimal 00 (the capture lost the subscript's form).
The starting address is fetched from the restart vector: PC takes the contents of FFFE and FFFF.
The processor is initialized (required after power-on) to start program execution.
The Condition Codes line of RESTART reads: Not affected.
The addressing mode of RESTART is extended indirect.
device_reset stores VECTOR_RESET_FFFE (0xFFFE in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea and calls reset_state, which sets m_state to 1, the state of INTERRUPT_VECTOR.
INTERRUPT_VECTOR loads PC high and low from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), reading memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, but calls the bound vector callback instead when one is set.
INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
device_reset also clears m_free_run.
The NMI vector location is FFFC (MS byte) and FFFD (LS byte).
NMI sets E, which the document glosses as the entire state being saved.
NMI stores to the stack, in this order, PCL, PCH, USL, USH, IYL, IYH, IXL, IXH, DPR, ACCB, ACCA and CCR (the capture reads DPR as OPR).
NMI sets I and F; the document says this masks interrupts.
Program control is transferred through the NMI vector; the operation line gives its first address as FFFC (the capture misreads the second).
A negative edge on the NMI input starts the NMI sequence at the end of the current instruction.
All of the processor's registers except the hardware stack pointer are pushed onto the hardware stack.
Successive negative edges on the NMI input cause successive NMI operations.
A RESET operation can internally block NMI operation.
If NMI was blocked, it occurs after the first load into the stack pointer (the capture reads LDS as lOS; TFR r,s; EXG r,s; etc.) after RESET.
Any non-maskable interrupt that occurs while NMI is blocked is latched.
The Condition Codes line of NMI reads: Not affected.
The addressing mode of NMI is inherent.
The NMI label stores VECTOR_NMI (0xFFFC in the enum) into m_ea through set_ea; MAIN jumps to it when get_pending_interrupt returns VECTOR_NMI.
The label continues at INTERRUPT_VECTOR: PC high and low come from read_vector(0) and read_vector(1), memory at m_ea.w plus the ordinal, or the bound vector callback when one is set.
The NMI label calls standard_irq_callback with INPUT_LINE_NMI and the PC.
The label calls dummy_read_opcode_arg(0) twice and dummy_vma(1) once, and INTERRUPT_VECTOR calls dummy_vma(1) twice.
m_lds_encountered is set in LD16 and LEA_us when S is selected, and in TFR for destination 4; the EXG body, cited whole, has no store of it.
device_reset clears m_lds_encountered, and execute_set_input sets m_nmi_asserted from an edge only when it is true, so earlier edges leave only m_nmi_line changed.
